summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a male with a history of dilated cardiomyopathy, type 2 diabetes, chronic kidney disease, and coronary artery disease, was admitted for substernal chest pain occurring ten days after placement of a drug-eluting stent in the left circumflex artery. The chest pain was likely related to non-adherence to clopidogrel due to a pharmacy hold on his account, which prevented him from filling the prescription. He was found to have stable cardiac enzymes with no evidence of acute infarction, mild pulmonary edema on imaging, and no recurrent symptoms during admission. He was restarted on clopidogrel and high-dose atorvastatin, with reinforcement of medication adherence. His heart failure regimen was optimized with torsemide 40 mg daily, and he remained in stable condition. He was discharged home with clear instructions on medication compliance, daily weight monitoring, and follow-up care.
